note: Verse text for the Surasamharam film's cards. Tamil lines are cut by code from the Project Madurai e-texts named here (rule 2: nobody types a verse by hand) and were compared by eye with the Tamil printed in Chelliah's book. Chelliah's English was transcribed from the page scans and must be proofread against them.

tmp46.author: Nakkirar
en: He plunged once in the cold and rock-girt sea
And made it much disturbed, and the giant killed
With long and flaming leaf-shaped spear.
tmp46.en_source: J. V. Chelliah, Pattupattu: Ten Tamil Idylls (1946; Tamil University reprint 1985), p. 343, his lines 70-72. Scan: https://archive.org/details/pattupattutentamilidyllschelliahj.v._108_Q (PDF page 374)

tmp59.author: Nakkirar
en: That wields the javelin red … dims their glory great by cutting down
Their ancient mango tree upon whose boughs
Hang downward bunches thick of blossoms bright.
tmp59.en_source: J. V. Chelliah, as above, p. 345, his lines 88-94, abridged where the ellipses stand. PDF page 376

kp492.author: Kachiyappa Sivachariyar
kp492.lines: Yuddha Kandam, Surapadman Vathai Padalam, verse 492
ta: தாவடி நெடுவேல் மீளத் தற்பரன் வரத்தால் வீடா
மேவலன் எழுந்து மீட்டும் மெய்பகிர் இரண்டு கூறுஞ்
சேவலும் மயிலு மாகிச் சினங்கொடு தேவர் சேனை
காவலன் தன்னை நாடி அமர்த்தொழில் கருதி வந்தான்.
en: When the long spear turned back, the foe, deathless by the Supreme One's boon, rose once more;
the two halves of his cloven body became a rooster and a peacock,
and in fury he came seeking the commander of the gods' army, set on battle.
kp492.en_source: Our own rendering (rule 3 as extended by AK, 16 Nov 2026); the reviewer must check it.
kp492.src_line: Kanda Puranam, Surapadman Vathai Padalam 492 · OUR RENDERING
